properties.name: The negative space becomes recordable — and readable
properties.rationale:
ALL THREE LEGS, DELIBERATELY, because the surface audit run hours earlier (`fact:the-three-legs-audit-run-at-last-...`) found 13 declared types with NO legs at all and five carrying all three and still unused. Shipping a writer without a reader would have added to that count on the same day the count was taken. The reader is the leg that kills vocabulary when it is missing: `DECOMPOSES` reached ZERO edges while shipping a detector for them, and a record nothing reads back is a record nobody writes twice.

⭐ A TEST FAILED FOR THE RIGHT REASON AND MOVED THE DESIGN. "A report may not name a tool reflow2 does not serve" was written into the CORE suite and failed there — the core does not know what the surface serves, and answering it there would have meant a second copy of the tool list maintained by hand, which is the defect class this project fixed three times the same day. The check moved to the tool, where `tool_router.has_route()` asks the LIVE ROUTER: nothing maintained, nothing that can drift. Both files carry a note saying why the test lives where it does, so the layering is not rediscovered later as an accident.

WHY THE DIAGNOSIS IS CLOSED: it is the one field that separates "nothing does this" from "something does and I did not find it" — a feature to build versus a feature to surface. `dec:bl-155`'s central finding is that reflow2 cannot otherwise tell unused from unreachable. Free text would let that distinction rot one report at a time, so an unknown value is refused and the refusal names what would have worked. `unknown` is kept as a legitimate answer because forcing a guess corrupts the other three.

🛑 TWO LIMITS RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED. First, it depends on the agent having NOTICED the tool existed, which is the same blind spot it exists to see — so an empty report is never evidence that nothing was hand-rolled, and the reader's own description says so. Second, `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` argues a tool is the wrong shape at all: "a tool must be CALLED, and the population most worth measuring is precisely the one least likely to call it." That is right, and here unavoidable: the server observes CALLS, and work done by hand happens where it cannot look. Asking is the only route that exists.

🛑 AND THE REPORT MUST NEVER BECOME TELEMETRY. `what` is free text naming the user's own domain — precisely the field `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` warns that "the next contributor will put something useful in". The prohibition is written into the module header, the tool description AND the skill, because those are the three places somebody wiring telemetry would look.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `report_manual_work` and `manual_work_report` added, plus a `capture-session` section asking the question at session end. Delivers `req:a-session-says-what-it-did-by-hand-that-reflow2-already-serves`. `report_manual_work` is the FIRST typed writer for a TemporalFact — a type with 304 instances here and, until now, no tool at all, so every one went through the `create_node` escape hatch. The `diagnosis` set is CLOSED and an unknown value is refused: `tool_missing` / `tool_not_found` / `tool_refused` / `unknown`. The same work reported twice is one record, since the id derives from `what`. Workspace suite 1824 passed / 0 failed across 161 binaries, reconciling exactly against 1817 + 7 new across 159 + 2 binaries; fmt, clippy, skill_lint clean; 163 toolsnaps.
